name: Airport Luggage
description: Size the market for checked and carry-on luggage.
formula: SAM = Population x Penetration Rate x Purchase Frequency x Average Spend x Serviceable %
solution_logic: Step 1: Identify addressable population = target_population x addressable_segment
Step 2: Apply penetration rate = addressable_population x penetration_rate
Step 3: Calculate annual spend per user = purchase_frequency x avg_spend_per_purchase
Step 4: Calculate TAM = penetrating_users x annual_spend_per_user
Step 5: Calculate SAM = TAM x serviceable_pct
key_insight: Market sizing is about defensible assumptions, not precision. Show your logic clearly -- the interviewer is testing your structure, not your arithmetic.
common_mistakes: Sizing the total population instead of the addressable segment
Forgetting purchase frequency -- confusing annual vs per-transaction spend
Not sanity-checking the output against known benchmarks
framework_soundbite: Top-down or bottom-up -- pick one, state your assumptions, and sanity-check the output. The logic matters more than the number.
business_contexts: a travel goods brand evaluating expansion into airport retail
a luggage manufacturer sizing replacement demand
question_patterns: A travel goods brand is deciding whether to open stores inside major airports and wants to size the serviceable portion of annual luggage replacement demand it could realistically reach.

prompts.advanced: A legacy luggage manufacturer facing declining mall traffic is considering a pivot into airport retail, but its board is skeptical the replacement cycle is long enough to support the real estate cost. Size the serviceable addressable market to inform the decision.
prompts.beginner: Estimate the serviceable addressable market for checked luggage purchases within major airport retail locations.
